text:
emily: heads-up — I kicked off a thread because we keep arguing about whether to trust real-traffic replay or synthetic rigs for our latency SLO work. can we land on a practical methodology? :thinking:
raj: short answer: both. long answer: depends on what you're measuring. replay nails cache/KV locality, synthetic is better for isolating batching/kernel effects.
marta: we had a case where replay masked a kernel regression because the replay traffic had unusually high prefix reuse. perf looked fine in replay, broke in prod.
chris: exact example?
marta: deploy-2026-02-14 — p99 spiked on one model. replay runs (from recorded traffic) showed nominal p99, synthetic microbatch sweep exposed extra tail at certain batch sizes.
yuki: that matches my profiling: mismatch happened when the kernel choice switched to int8-fused GEMM on long sequences. throughput improved, but tail grew due to a rare slow path in the kernel when occupancy dropped.
emily: so replay hid it because the KV cache hits kept average seq len low?
yuki: yup. KV cache locality kept actual per-request work lower and avoided the long-sequence slow path. synthetic tests that forced longer sequences expose it.
raj: implications: when we benchmark microbatch sizing against p95/p99 we need two axes: realistic mix (replay) and stress sweep (synthetic). Treat them as separate objectives, not a single number.
chris: agreed. propose this: 1) run nightly replay to catch behavioral regressions tied to actual traffic; 2) run synthetic sweep matrix (batch sizes 1,2,4,8,16; sequence lengths 64,256,1024) to map kernel boundaries and tail effects; 3) add KV-hit/miss controlled runs to measure cache sensitivity.
marta: addendum: for synthetic sweeps, randomize arrival jitter to simulate queueing and microbatch formation. pure constant-rate load hides burst-induced batching differences.
emily: good point. something like: `wrk -t12 -c256 -d60s --arrival-jitter=exp` (pseudo) or our internal runner with poisson arrival.
perf-bot: CI alert — nightly replay job `replay/nightly-main` completed. no regression detected. baseline p99=210ms.
raj: the CI replay is necessary but we should also gate changes with a small synthetic perf job that runs the sweep. otherwise kernel swaps sneak in during merges.
ysuki: (typo: yuki) +1 — we need an automated microbatch/seq sweep in the PR perf checklist. a failing condition: any p99 increase > 5% at any sweep point.
chris: quick question on metrics: do we report p95 and p99 absolute numbers or deltas vs baseline? deltas are easier for CI but ops want absolute SLOs in dashboards.
emily: both. CI uses deltas to detect regressions quickly. dashboards show absolute p95/p99 along with a colored band for SLO.
marta: also include tail-latency distributions — not just single quantiles. e.g., 99.9th or a small histogram bucket, because some kernel issues show as a heavy tail beyond p99.
raj: can we instrument kernel selection boundaries in the trace? so a spike can be correlated with "kernel=X" decision and microbatch size?
yuki: yes — runtime already tags `kernel_variant` in traces. we should add microbatch_size and kv_hit_rate per request. then replay/traces can be sliced.
emily: next steps: chris to add synthetic sweep job to PR perf checks; raj to update nightly pipeline to include KV-controlled replay variants; yuki to add microbatch/kv tags to traces; marta to document the methodology and pass criteria.
chris: I'll draft the PR job YAML. quick sketch: `matrix: {batch_size: [1,2,4,8,16], seq_len: [64,256,1024], kv_rate: [0.9,0.5,0.1]}` run for 30s each, collect p95/p99 and histogram.
ysuki: make sure to randomize request arrival so microbatch formation is realistic. include a seed so runs are reproducible.
perf-bot: note: perf regression in a recent PRs happened because a kernel fallback path triggered under low occupancy. repro steps attached in `perf/bugs/2026-02-kernel-fallback`.
emily: thanks perf-bot. last point — measurement math: use inverse-cdf method for quantiles with reservoir sampling on streams, to avoid bias in long runs. we had a bad episode where subsampling biased p99 down.
raj: good call. and for reporting, show both sample-corrected quantiles and raw counts. auditors hate black-box numbers.
marta: I'll start the doc in docs/perf/methodology.md and link real repros and scripts. ping me if you want to co-author.
emily: awesome — let's reconvene next week after the PR job is up. :thumbsup:
